the current session\\n\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\n\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\n\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker's assigned path and permissions. |\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker's terminal state after stop. |\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\n\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\n\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\n\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\n\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\n\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\n\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e 'const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\"python3\\\",\\\"-B\\\",\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\",\\\"--root\\\",\\\".\\\",\\\"--commit\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\"1\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\n\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\n\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\n\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case's expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\n\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\n\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. See the [structured method contract](orchestration-contract.md). All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"references/model-roles.md\",\n    \"sha256\": \"c86696b6c568b7db80a7e339856986e64482ce6a418bb91946ce3a3b772f79a1\",\n    \"bytes\": 2869,\n    \"text\": \"# Model selection for portable roles\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. These [poteto](agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and [comment reviewer](agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) prompts are instructions supplied to an exposed worker operation. Reading them does not register a custom agent or authorize delegation.\\n\\n| Role | Default requested model | Observed model | Supported effort | Fallback disclosure |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| poteto-agent | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n| comment-sicko | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n\\nFor each assignment, record requested model and effort, observed model and effort, supported effort values and their source, worker identity, and fallback disclosure. Use `unknown` for information the operation does not expose. `inherit-parent` records a selection policy, not an observed model name. Do not silently convert a requested model into an actual model.\\n\\nSelect an explicit model only from current exposed tool documentation or observed enumeration results. If enumeration is missing, disclose that limit and retain `inherit-parent`. Documentation examples are not a list of available models. Use only an effort supported for the selected model by the current operation; do not carry an incompatible inherited effort into an explicit selection.\\n\\nIf a selected model or effort is rejected, retain the rejection. Use an authorized inherited or supported alternative only after disclosing the changed selection. If the task requires that exact selection, stop and record blocked. A fallback never proves the original selection succeeded.\\n\\nIdentical observed models mean no model diversity. Different roles can supply distinct instructions on the same model. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified, even when requested model names differ. Different observed models support a model-diversity statement only for those observed assignments. Worker independence still requires successful spawn and result inspection.\\n\\nWhen workers are unavailable, apply an authorized role sequentially and label reduced capability. Preserve scope and permission boundaries. Do not claim independent review, background execution, or full worker support from sequential role switching.\\n\\nThe cached documentation from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents describes inheritance and optional local agent configuration. It is context only. This package writes no local custom-agent configuration and claims no current host model or worker support from that documentation.\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"references/orchestration-contract.md\",\n    \"sha256\": \"5dd740ad66d992df252754d189d0dc207900023372392a0db4309b85eb5e4ec5\",\n    \"bytes\": 6273,\n    \"text\": \"# Assignment and integration contract\\n\\nBefore dispatch, the coordinator creates an immutable assignment with `id`, `scope`, `inputRevision`, `outputOwner`, `isolatedOutputPath`, `role`, `retryCount`, `terminalStatus`, and `evidenceLinks`. Use the full Git SHA for inputRevision, an exact owned path, and an explicit role. Start retryCount at 0 and terminalStatus at `pending`. Preserve every attempt as an append-only event under the same assignment ID; update status through events, never rewrite the original scope, revision, owner or path. A changed scope or revision requires a new assignment ID that links its predecessor.\\n\\nThe coordinator checks authorization and observed host bindings before dispatch. One path has one writer. Reject overlapping paths before work starts; assign distinct paths instead. Workers write only their isolated output and report results. Only the coordinator integrates shared files, inventory, registry, or other workers' output.\\n\\nAccept a result only when its assignment identity and input SHA match, its artifacts exist, and required method evidence was observed. Reject stale revisions. Permit at most one retry for missing required SHA or method evidence, after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming the same permissions still apply. A retry count of 1 exhausts this allowance. Denied permissions, unknown action outcomes, and missing artifacts never become success by retry policy.\\n\\nTerminal states are `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A completion event links the exact result and evidence. Stop a cancelled worker through the exposed stop binding when available, then inspect its terminal state. Quarantine any partial artifacts; cancellation does not authorize their integration. If stop cannot be observed, record that limit and do not claim termination. Report interrupted execution explicitly.\\n\\nBefore an external action, record explicit permission, a stable action identity, the intended destination and the last observed outcome. After interruption, inspect whether that identity already completed. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to the destination. If the outcome is unknown, block replay. Do not infer permission from upstream autonomy instructions.\\n\\nHistory and persistence have separate bindings. Keep assignment events and result links in an authorized durable location and verify readback. If unavailable, declare the gap and offer an authorized local handoff as reduced capability; never claim unattended recovery or cross-session continuity. All host statuses remain `not-run` until actual observations exist.\\n\\n## Structured Arena and Swarm receipts\\n\\nA method receipt is JSON with schemaVersion 1, kind `arena` or `swarm`, inputRevision, assignments, reviewArtifact, reviewedBy and declaredOrder. The inputRevision is the actual task repository revision, distinct from the packageCommit identifying these instructions. It must match the evidence record. The declared order precedes every dispatch. reviewArtifact records the qualitative outcome review and reviewedBy identifies its reviewer. All referenced artifacts must exist and be listed in the evidence record.\\n\\nEach assignment records id, workerId, inputRevision, outputOwner, outputPath, role, status, startedOrder, completedOrder, requestedModel, actualModel, retryCount, method, taskArtifact, rubricProvided, resultRevision, resultMethod and outputSha256. Result revision and method must match the assignment, and the inspected output bytes must match their digest. Worker and assignment identities are distinct. outputOwner equals workerId; output directories do not overlap. Integer order values record the observed dispatch and completion sequence, not estimated time. The method has positive sampleCount, sampleDefinition and order. Missing model observations use unknown. The validator requires assignment-bound spawn and result inspection, and isolated-write for output-producing candidates. A read-only judge may return its result through the coordinator's authorized artifact capture. A cancelled result needs bound stop, terminal inspection and quarantine observations. No operation string alone establishes a method.\\n\\nArena adds candidates, judge, rubricArtifact and synthesis. At least two candidates share the same taskArtifact, finish before a distinct fresh judge starts and do not receive the parent rubric. Synthesis has order, inspectedCandidates, artifact and verificationArtifact; it follows completed judgment and accounts for every candidate. The review artifact assesses scoring, base selection, grafts, rejections and verification quality. File presence and phase ordering do not establish the quality of those decisions.\\n\\nSwarm adds partition, race, cancelled and quarantined. Partition declares requiredSlices, results mapping each slice to its assignment, and gaps. A full coverage claim requires all slices with completed inspected outputs; gaps remain explicit reduced or blocked work. Race declares rule, assignments, winner and ruleArtifact. first-pass must select the first completed survivor; rank-all needs all results; best-of retains an explicit reviewed selection. Cancelled assignments must be quarantined and cannot enter the aggregate. The combined partition-and-race case requires both methods and its cancellation exercise. The partition walkthrough exercises only its declared slices; it does not acquire an unrelated race requirement.\\n\\nThe three-file Swarm walkthrough requires exactly three declared slices and three completed results. Its partition-only receipt uses race null and empty cancellation, quarantine and failureExercises arrays. The combined case also records failureExercises. Each event has assignmentId, kind, attempt, order, reason and evidence, with bound result-rejection or terminal inspection. Rejected missing-revision or missing-method evidence uses attempts 0 then 1; a second invalid result exhausts the retry and leaves a failed or blocked assignment. A separate failed or blocked dropout is disclosed. These failed outputs cannot satisfy required coverage. The final assignment result metadata records the inspected terminal summary; rejection-event artifacts retain the invalid attempts.\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"references/workflow-ownership.md\",\n    \"sha256\": \"50644b3a9a3dfd5651382eaca1d3a2728af0b3157d6d66b730930370a64bb03c\",\n    \"bytes\": 1265,\n    \"text\": \"# Workflow ownership\\n\\nAn explicit pstack invocation gives pstack ownership of that workflow. An explicit Superpowers invocation gives Superpowers ownership. Do not run both controllers over the same assignment or let one silently replace the other's plan, review, or integration decisions.\\n\\nFor an unqualified request, D1 retains the already active workflow. With no active workflow, use host defaults and do not activate either orchestration mode automatically. If both pstack and Superpowers are explicitly requested, clarify ownership before launching workers or changing artifacts. Preserve the active controller across follow-ups unless the user changes ownership. A helper skill can advise the owner without becoming a second controller.\\n\\nThe owner assigns one coordinator. Workers produce isolated artifacts and evidence; the coordinator reviews and integrates them. Shared inventory and registry writes belong to the coordinator. Worker cancellation, stale results or unavailable tools do not transfer that ownership automatically.\\n\\nHost permissions and user authorization constrain every owner. Local structural tests, documented APIs and declared cases provide no host pass. Explicit reduced or blocked results remain visible beside the full expectation.\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"docs/setup/chatgpt.md\",\n    \"sha256\": \"4c656ee873b5182e975bbf232988220440c5107db9a1b996185bcd56a4019753\",\n    \"bytes\": 2864,\n    \"text\": \"# Personal ChatGPT setup\\n\\nStarting state for `chatgpt-setup-from-readme` is an ordinary personal ChatGPT conversation with no observed pstack loading. The personal route is unsupported here and explicitly blocked. Do not turn a local filesystem path into a universal ChatGPT installation step.\\n\\nOfficial guidance describes packaging a skills-only plugin, installing it from a local source and testing in a new enabled conversation. It does not establish that this personal conversation exposes that route. Checked 2026-10-08. [Official complete-plugin testing](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/connect-chatgpt).\\n\\n1. From [README](../../README.md), open this guide and [compatibility](../compatibility.md). Inspect actual plugin controls and tools read-only.\\n2. Record missing or denied loading and discovery operations. Stop the setup branch if the route is absent, or if installation, enabling or settings are not explicitly authorized. Do not add an MCP service to make this skills-only package appear supported.\\n3. For an authorized explanation, supply the exact relevant skill and its required references in the conversation. Follow [workflow selection](../workflows/choosing-a-workflow.md). Label this supplied-source use reduced capability. It is not installed package discovery, persistent activation, independent execution or a host pass.\\n4. If a supported route is later exposed and separately authorized, use the actual host controls and a fresh chat. Record `discover-package`, `enumerate-skills` and `inspect-installed-copy` with observed tool identifiers and artifact evidence. Require all 51 root names, exact installed-copy identity, package version and final frozen SHA, plus the three canonical nested Benny exclusions. Read [inventory](../parity/inventory.json) and [catalog](../skills/README.md) as comparison data only.\\n5. Run the [six walkthrough cases](../parity/cases/documentation-walkthroughs.json) and record actual outputs under the [host contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Workers, execution, persistence, models and integrations need separate exposed and successful bindings. A conversation without them leaves dependent gates blocked.\\n\\nExpected visible result today is an explicit setup/discovery block and a bounded explanation if source is supplied. A future complete installed receipt can change that status only after fresh observations. The [Codex guide](codex.md) describes a different documented route. Its local path and cache rules do not establish personal ChatGPT support.\\n\\n[Optional development dependencies](../testing/helper-setup.md) are separate from host installation. No generic setup permission follows from their historical snapshot approval. Refresh or removal requires an observed host control and exact authorization; neither source edits nor removing supplied text proves uninstall.\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"docs/setup/codex.md\",\n    \"sha256\": \"29386cd7894bb56a36ae1285fa005f3794050a017e6eb07000440a9dd80c42f8\",\n    \"bytes\": 3373,\n    \"text\": \"# Codex setup\\n\\nStarting state for `codex-setup-from-readme` is a fresh chat without approved pstack loading. This route is documented, unverified for this package and blocked until exact setup authorization and fresh discovery evidence exist.\\n\\nCurrent official guidance describes local marketplace installation. A repo marketplace uses `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and a relative `source.path` inside its marketplace root. Restart the Codex desktop app, select that source in the Plugins Directory, install, then start a new enabled chat. The host loads a cached installed copy. Refresh can replace that copy; disabling does not remove it. Follow the current removal control and inspect its result before claiming removal. Source edits alone do not refresh a chat. This saved source review covers the Codex desktop Plugins Directory. Other clients remain unverified. These are documentation facts, not observed access in this account. Checked 2026-10-08. [Official packaging](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins).\\n\\n1. From [README](../../README.md), open this guide and [compatibility](../compatibility.md). Record the candidate version from [plugin.json](../../plugin.json) and full final frozen Git SHA.\\n2. Inspect the host's actual plugin controls read-only. If no local source or plugin control exists, record blocked. Do not silently copy individual skills or change personal configuration to claim package loading.\\n3. Before any setup, obtain explicit authorization for the exact package copy, marketplace file, cache and settings changes, app restart, install and enable scope. This guide is not that authorization. No marketplace is created by this package.\\n4. Only within that approved scope, follow the documented local route above. Verify the installed copy through the actual host operation, not a direct repository read. Start a fresh chat after loading.\\n5. Observe `discover-package`, `enumerate-skills` and `inspect-installed-copy`. Retain the tool identifiers and evidence artifacts. Compare every root name to the [51-skill catalog](../skills/README.md). Exclude the three nested Benny skill paths in [inventory](../parity/inventory.json). Record the actual installed identity, version and exact frozen SHA in a discovery receipt.\\n6. Run the representative [walkthrough cases](../parity/cases/documentation-walkthroughs.json) with [session bindings](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Independent workers need spawn and inspected results. Unknown models remain unknown. Complete direct discovery can pass without workers. A fallback omitting a task requirement is reduced capability and still cannot weaken installed-copy identity or enumeration.\\n\\nUse the [helper guide](../testing/helper-setup.md) only for separately authorized development validation. Missing dependencies block helper-backed work. No dependency install, integration, MCP, lifecycle hook or model persistence is needed merely to read the catalog.\\n\\nExpected visible result is a host-observed installed package with all 51 roots and exact identity, followed by inspected walkthrough artifacts. Without it, loading and discovery remain blocked or not-run. Supplied-source explanations are reduced capability and prove no registration. [Test matrix](../testing/host-matrix.md) defines later host evidence; [troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md) bounds failures.\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"docs/compatibility.md\",\n    \"sha256\": \"085c37d688a912c023ff155e0020945fddd7d436f20cf4cd3197a17a5835c01f\",\n    \"bytes\": 3062,\n    \"text\": \"# Candidate compatibility\\n\\nThis is an evidence-bounded candidate summary, not a list of assumed product tools. Current [inventory](parity/inventory.json) records both hosts as not-run. Installed discovery is absent and required host validation is pending. Local source inspection, schema checks and helper fixtures prove no host loading or behavioral parity.\\n\\n| Host or operation | Candidate status | Evidence needed |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Personal ChatGPT loading | Unsupported route, explicitly blocked | Actual supported loading control, exact separate setup authorization and fresh complete discovery |\\n| Codex loading | Documented route, unverified and undiscovered | Actual installed-copy operation, full 51-root enumeration, version and final frozen SHA |\\n| Independent Arena or Swarm | Not-run on both hosts | Authorized observed spawn, terminal results and inspected artifacts |\\n| Sequential supplied-source work | Possible reduced branch, not a recorded pass | Actual authorized reads and artifacts, required observations and complete discovery for package acceptance |\\n| Dependency-backed helpers | Setup-required in operative candidate | Exact local dependency metadata and caller-specific execution evidence |\\n| Historical helper validation | Passed only in isolated snapshot | [Helper guide](testing/helper-setup.md) identifies the exact tested source SHA and limits |\\n| Optional integrations and Benny | Not-run or blocked when unavailable | [Benny readiness](testing/benny-readiness.md), actual bindings and separate action permission |\\n\\nUse [host matrix](testing/host-matrix.md), [case registry](parity/case-registry.json), [case schema](parity/cases/schema.json) and [evidence schema](parity/evidence.schema.json). Required cases need actual host observations or explicit blocked records. Complete discovery needs the identical 51-root receipt in a direct pass, worker pass or validated sequential reduced-pass. A reduction never proves worker independence or full orchestration.\\n\\n[Release report](../tools/release_report.py) checks actual root evidence and discovery. The [marker contract](maintenance/rollback.md) permits only explicit narrow report paths and verification changes. Full tracked bytes and modes, including setup and navigation, must match. After blocked records merge and catalog regeneration changes operative catalog bytes, take an explicit second freeze and attach fresh blocked discovery observations to its exact SHA. Preserve both freeze SHAs and earlier records in Git history. The final handoff navigation must be a no-op unless explicitly refrozen; no evidence pass is inherited.\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  },\n  {\n    \"path\": \"docs/testing/helper-setup.md\",\n    \"sha256\": \"124697022f3133a225be940cd1c6e5d832d65f12ddef70689567d9717cec216e\",\n    \"bytes\": 5369,\n    \"text\": \"# Helper dependency setup\\n\\nBootstrap checks the local [manifest](../../skills/poteto-mode/scripts/package.json), [lock](../../skills/poteto-mode/scripts/bun.lock) and installed package metadata. Missing, unreadable or mismatched files cause a setup-required error and nonzero exit. [ensureDependenciesInstalled](../../skills/poteto-mode/scripts/bootstrap.ts) never installs, spawns, restarts or writes. Use Bun with runtime auto-install disabled.\\n\\n## Exact historical approved scope\\n\\nThe separately approved validation copy was the complete committed snapshot `37b68c8e842b275f310ead112c0ecb7fa0ade308` at `/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-openai-helper-verification`. It was created only after verifying that directory was absent. Its install working directory was `/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-openai-helper-verification/skills/poteto-mode/scripts`. Its cache was `/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-openai-helper-verification/.bun-cache`.\\n\\nThe pins are commander 14.0.0, bun-types 1.3.14 and typescript 7.0.2. Reconciliation changed only the two workspace devDependency requests from latest to the existing exact pins. All 25 package records, transitive requests, platform conditions and integrity values remained byte-identical. These include @types/node 26.1.2, undici-types 8.3.0 and TypeScript platform packages 7.0.2. The operative lock now includes the reviewed request reconciliation. It has SHA-256 `530b7fb6cba7f0b2a6cfc862dbcfe9020c333d45e7e0f448133006583ffdc1f2`. The original lock hash was `667d9cf7222e9aae3fa42a4be383e657784216e9df115da02227fbc5ac7bbe46`.\\n\\n## Procedure for a separately authorized copy\\n\\nNo generic new setup authorization follows from that historical approval. Before future setup, agree an exact immutable source SHA, complete writable copy, absent destination, scripts cwd, task-owned cache and allowed writes. Do not install in a host cache or operative invocation. Use existing Bun. Missing Bun or unavailable exact pins stops the procedure. No substitutes or material resolution/integrity changes are allowed without new review.\\n\\nA reconciliation install, only if specifically needed and authorized, must use `bun install --ignore-scripts --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org --cache-dir=<approved-task-cache>` from the approved scripts cwd. Review any manifest/lock diff before frozen verification. Preserve every direct pin and all 25 transitive/integrity records. The current operative lock already has reconciled requests, so ordinary execution does not regenerate it.\\n\\nFor the historically approved snapshot, the actual frozen install command was:\\n\\n```sh\\nbun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org --cache-dir=/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-openai-helper-verification/.bun-cache\\n```\\n\\nIt ran from the exact scripts cwd above. It contacted the explicit registry, downloaded packages and wrote snapshot node_modules and its cache. Lifecycle scripts were disabled. No global settings/cache, credentials or operative source writes were approved. A future exact-copy approval must specify its own scope rather than reuse these paths or overwrite this snapshot.\\n\\n## Historical observed validation\\n\\nBun 1.4.2 revision `50a8a838737a8f0e226d1c115788aa18192a2f18` completed the reviewed frozen install. These commands then ran from that snapshot's scripts cwd:\\n\\n```sh\\nbun --no-install -e 'import {ensureDependenciesInstalled} from \\\"./bootstrap.ts\\\"; ensureDependenciesInstalled()'\\nORCH_TEST_ROOT=/Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-openai-helper-test-scratch bun --no-install test bootstrap.test.ts orch watch-pr\\nbun --no-install node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --project watch-pr/tsconfig.json --noEmit --strict\\n```\\n\\nBootstrap passed. The suites passed 85 tests with 316 assertions and zero failures across five files. Strict TypeScript exited 0 without diagnostics. Tests used inert bootstrap spies, injected watcher transports, fake Graphite and owned fixture repositories. No live gh ran. All 299 tracked snapshot files matched the source commit except the reviewed two-request lock reconciliation. Tests and installation preserved the reviewed lock bytes.\\n\\nThe operative candidate has no installed dependencies. Snapshot results support only that source snapshot, not this caller, the current package or either host. Missing current metadata leaves dependency-backed helpers blocked. Development dependency setup is separate from plugin loading, enabling, integration, credentials and host behavior. See [Codex setup](../setup/codex.md), [ChatGPT setup](../setup/chatgpt.md) and [compatibility](../compatibility.md).\\n\\n## Offline maintenance source input\\n\\nSource-inventory tests need the exact canonical subtree as local data. Set `PSTACK_SOURCE_FIXTURE` to its absolute directory when it is outside the previously retained research tree beneath your home Herd directory. Run maintenance tests through Bun with Python bytecode disabled:\\n\\n```sh\\nPSTACK_SOURCE_FIXTURE=/absolute/path/to/pinned/pstack bun --no-install -e 'const r=Bun.spawnSync([\\\"python3\\\",\\\"-B\\\",\\\"-m\\\",\\\"unittest\\\",\\\"discover\\\",\\\"-s\\\",\\\"tests\\\",\\\"-v\\\"],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\"1\\\"},stdout:\\\"inherit\\\",stderr:\\\"inherit\\\"});process.exit(r.exitCode)'\\n```\\n\",\n    \"binary\": false\n  }\n]"

      "text": "export function calculate(rows){return rows.reduce((n,r)=>n+r.qty*r.unitPrice,0)}\nexport function adapter(invoice){return calculate(invoice.rows)}\nexport function facade(invoice){return adapter(invoice)}\nexport function controller(invoice){return {total:facade(invoice)}}\nexport function format(n){if(!Number.isFinite(n))throw new Error(\"nonfinite\");return n.toFixed(2)}\n"

Everything else is meat.\n\n`eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, and similar suppressions stink. Look up the rule. If it catches real bugs or protects correctness or safety, remove the suppression within the authorized comment scope and mark the exact guilty symbol `MUST KILL`.\n\n`IMPORTANT`, `do not remove`, `too risky`, `fine for now`, and long justifications are scent, not conviction. Before judging, read nearby code. If its claim is not obvious there, run `/how`, `/why`, or both using the [how](../../skills/how/SKILL.md) and [why](../../skills/why/SKILL.md) skills on the named symbol or call. Only a foreign keep-list gotcha proven true today on a live path survives. Our-code surprises die with the reshape flag above. Doubt after the hunt is meat.\n\nIf code, a rule, or a required investigative skill cannot be inspected, report the missing evidence as a skip. Delete the comment within the authorized scope. Never polish meat into a shorter alibi. Mark the exact guilty symbol `MUST KILL`. My deletion ends there. I do not reshape the application code.\n\nEvery flag names code inside the scope and tells the truth. I invent nothing. When scoped comment writes are authorized and available, I touch comments and identify refactor targets. I never write application code or perform the flagged refactors. The final response is a report only. Name actual touched files, actual deletion count, `MUST KILL` flags with one line each, and skips. Verify edits before counting them.\n\nWhen writes are unavailable, denied, or unauthorized, use an explicitly reduced read-only review if authorized. Make no edits. Name reviewed files and proposed deletions, keep the same scope and investigation rules, and state that the actual deletion count is zero. Do not report proposals as completed deletions. If the task requires actual edits and that reduced branch is not authorized, record blocked.\n\nFollow [model roles](../model-roles.md) and [session capabilities](../host-capabilities.md). This portable prompt does not register a custom agent. If independent workers are unavailable, authorized sequential review is reduced capability.       "sha256": "a5bdf441da297569830d37fe593899b409a82a104681464f4a6e93962a720327",

      "text": "# Reviewer Prompt Template\n\nBuild each reviewer subagent's prompt from this template, filling in the placeholders.\n\n---\n\nYou are an adversarial code reviewer. Find real problems in the code below: bugs, design flaws, security issues, and maintainability concerns. You are not here to be helpful or encouraging. You are here to stress-test.\n\n## Intent\n\nThe author's stated intent for this change:\n\n> Quote CSV fields containing commas, quotation marks, CR or LF and double embedded quotes while preserving String conversion, row/column order, CRLF row separators, plain values and empty exports. Only this actual supplied base-to-head patch is in scope; no source edits or external actions are authorized.\n\nYou are reviewing whether the code achieves this intent well. Do NOT question the intent itself. Assume the goal is correct and challenge the execution.\n\n## Code Under Review\n\nActual base 5151261871f115081448de84ea8d09ef468f4843, head 1445883fb60d9db45377a337390d3a775998e441. source.patch matched actual Git diff.\ndiff --git a/csv.mjs b/csv.mjs\nindex 16cfbcf..a6b9868 100644\n--- a/csv.mjs\n+++ b/csv.mjs\n@@ -1 +1,2 @@\n-export function csv(rows){return rows.map(row=>row.map(String).join(',')).join('\\r\\n');}\n+const quote=value=>{const text=String(value);return /[\",\\r\\n]/.test(text)?'\"'+text.replaceAll('\"','\"\"')+'\"':text;};\n+export function csv(rows){return rows.map(row=>row.map(quote).join(',')).join('\\r\\n');}\n\nComplete head csv.mjs:\nconst quote=value=>{const text=String(value);return /[\",\\r\\n]/.test(text)?'\"'+text.replaceAll('\"','\"\"')+'\"':text;};\nexport function csv(rows){return rows.map(row=>row.map(quote).join(',')).join('\\r\\n');}\n\nComplete csv.test.mjs:\nimport {test,expect} from 'bun:test';import {csv} from './csv.mjs';\ntest('literal spreadsheet quoting contract',()=>{expect(csv([['plain','with,comma','say \"hi\"','a\\r\\nb']])).toBe('plain,\"with,comma\",\"say \"\"hi\"\"\",\"a\\r\\nb\"');expect(csv([])).toBe('');expect(csv([[0,null],['x','y']])).toBe('0,null\\r\\nx,y');});\n\n\n## Review Rubric\n\n# Review Rubric\n\nReview through whichever lenses are relevant. Not every lens applies to every change. Use judgment.\n\n## Correctness\n\nDoes the code actually do what the intent says it should?\n\n- Edge cases: empty inputs, nil/undefined, boundary values, concurrent access\n- Error handling: are errors caught, propagated, or silently swallowed?\n- Off-by-one, type coercion, integer overflow, string encoding\n- State management: race conditions, stale closures, dangling references\n- Does the happy path work? Does the sad path work?\n- Idempotency: what happens if this operation runs twice, or if a previous run crashed halfway? If the answer is \"it depends on what state was left behind,\" there's a missing reconciliation step.\n- Concurrency: if multiple actors can touch the same mutable state (files, branches, shared data), is access serialized structurally (locks, sequential phases, exclusive ownership), or by conventions that won't hold?\n\nWhen you find a potential bug, trace the execution path. Don't just flag \"this could be nil\". Show the call chain that makes it nil.\n\n## Root Causes vs. Symptoms\n\nIs the code fixing the actual problem or papering over a symptom?\n\nAnswering this often requires looking beyond the changed files. Read the surrounding code (callers, callees, type definitions, sibling modules) and understand the architecture the change lives in. Use the tools available to you (Read, Grep, Glob) to explore. Follow the call chain. Read the types. Understand why the code exists before judging whether the change addresses the right layer.\n\n- Guard clauses that mask a deeper invariant violation\n- Retry logic that hides a broken contract\n- Type casts that silence a modeling error\n- If you see a workaround, ask: why is the workaround needed? What would a proper fix look like?\n- A fix in module A that should really be a fix in module B's contract\n- Instructions where structure would be better: if the fix is a comment saying \"don't do X\" or a convention someone has to remember, ask whether it could instead be a type constraint, a lint rule, or a runtime check that makes the wrong thing impossible\n\n## Structural Integrity\n\nDoes the code fit well into the system it's part of?\n\n- Boundary discipline: is validation at system boundaries, or scattered through business logic? Validate data once where it enters the system, then trust it internally.\n- Abstraction level: is the code mixing high-level orchestration with low-level detail?\n- Coupling: does this change introduce dependencies that will make future changes harder?\n- Data model fit: do the data structures match the actual access patterns? The right structure makes downstream code obvious. The wrong one fights you at every turn.\n- Bolted-on vs. integrated: was the change patched onto the existing design, or does it read as if the design always accounted for it? If the new requirement had been known from the start, would the code look like this?\n- Legacy dual-paths: does the change introduce a new API while keeping the old one alive? If there are no external consumers, migrate callers and delete the old path in the same wave. Don't leave compatibility layers that will become permanent.\n\nDon't penalize simple code for lacking abstraction. Premature abstraction is worse than duplication.\n\n## Verification\n\nCan you tell that this code works from reading it?\n\n- Are there tests? Do they test behavior or implementation details?\n- Are there assertions/invariants that would catch regressions?\n- If this is a bug fix: is there a test for the bug?\n- If this touches an integration boundary: is the full path tested?\n- Check the real thing, not a proxy. If the code checks liveness via file mtime or cached state instead of reading the actual value, that's a verification gap.\n- For delegated or async work: does the code verify actual output artifacts, or does it trust self-reports and summaries?\n\n## Complexity Budget\n\nIs the complexity justified by what the code accomplishes?\n\n- Code that could be simpler without losing correctness or clarity\n- Abstractions that serve only one call site\n- Configuration or parameterization for cases that don't exist yet\n- Dead code, unused imports, vestigial parameters\n- Over-engineering: \"just in case\" code paths with no current callers\n- Obsolete compatibility paths kept alive for transitional stability that's no longer needed. If the migration is done, delete the scaffolding\n- Does the user experience justify the complexity? Every feature, control, and option should earn its place. Half-finished features are worse than missing ones.\n\nSimpler is better unless simpler is wrong. Three lines of duplication beat a premature abstraction.\n\n## Security\n\nFor each security finding, trace the input path through the code and show it.\n\n- User input flowing to dangerous sinks (SQL, shell, eval, innerHTML) without sanitization\n- Authentication/authorization gaps in new endpoints\n- Secrets in code, logs, or error messages\n- TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) in security-critical paths\n\n\n## Code Quality Lens\n\n# Code Quality Review\n\nEach reviewer applies this code-quality lens in addition to the rubric. It is a strict standard focused on implementation quality, maintainability, abstraction quality, and codebase health.\n\nAbove all, be ambitious about code structure. Do not merely identify local cleanup. Actively search for \"code judo\" moves, restructurings that preserve behavior while making the implementation dramatically simpler, smaller, more direct, and more elegant.\n\n## Core Prompt\n\nStart from this baseline:\n\n> Perform a deep code quality audit of the current branch's changes.\n> Rethink how to structure / implement the changes to meaningfully improve code quality without impacting behavior.\n> Work to improve abstractions, modularity, reduce Spaghetti code, improve succinctness and legibility.\n> Be ambitious, if there is a clear path to improving the implementation that involves restructuring some of the codebase, go for it.\n> Be extremely thorough and rigorous. Measure twice, cut once.\n\n## Dimensions\n\nEach dimension is stated once. Apply the ones that are relevant.\n\n0. **Be ambitious about structural simplification.** Do not stop at \"this could be a bit cleaner.\" Look for reframings that make whole branches, helpers, modes, conditionals, or layers disappear. Assume a \"code judo\" move is often available. It uses the existing architecture more effectively and makes the change dramatically simpler. If you can delete complexity rather than rearrange it, push hard for that.\n\n1. **Do not let a PR push a file from under 1k lines to over 1k lines without a very strong reason.** Treat this as a strong smell. Prefer extracting helpers, subcomponents, or modules. If the diff crosses that threshold, ask whether the code should be decomposed first. Waive only for a compelling structural reason where the resulting file stays clearly organized.\n\n2. **Do not allow spaghetti growth in existing code.** Be suspicious of new ad-hoc conditionals, scattered special cases, or one-off branches inserted into unrelated flows. Treat \"weird if statements in random places\" as a design problem, not a style nit. Prefer pushing the logic into a dedicated helper, state machine, or module instead of tangling an existing path.\n\n3. **Bias toward cleaning the design, not just accepting working code.** If behavior can stay the same while the structure becomes meaningfully cleaner, push for the cleaner version. Prefer simplifications that remove moving pieces over refactors that spread the same complexity around.\n\n4. **Prefer direct, boring, maintainable code over hacky or magical code.** Treat brittle, ad-hoc, or \"magic\" behavior as a problem. Be skeptical of generic mechanisms that hide simple data-shape assumptions. Flag thin abstractions, identity wrappers, or pass-through helpers that add indirection without buying clarity.\n\n5. **Push on type and boundary cleanliness when it affects maintainability.** Question unnecessary optionality, `unknown`, `any`, or cast-heavy code when a clearer type boundary could exist. Prefer explicit typed models over loosely-shaped ad-hoc objects. If a branch leans on a silent fallback to paper over an unclear invariant, ask whether the boundary should be made explicit.\n\n6. **Keep logic in the canonical layer and reuse existing helpers.** Call out feature logic leaking into shared paths or implementation details leaking through APIs. Prefer existing canonical utilities over bespoke one-offs. Push code toward the right package, service, or module instead of normalizing drift.\n\n7. **Treat unnecessary sequential orchestration and non-atomic updates as design smells when the cleaner structure is obvious.** If independent work is serialized for no reason, ask whether it should run in parallel. If related updates can leave state half-applied, push for a more atomic structure. Do not over-index on micro-optimizations, but do flag avoidable orchestration complexity that makes the code more brittle.\n\n## Output Expectations\n\nPrioritize structural code-quality regressions and missed simplifications first, then spaghetti and branching complexity, then boundary, type, and file-size concerns, then smaller modularity and legibility issues.\n\n## Approval Bar\n\nDo not approve merely because behavior seems correct. Treat these as presumptive blockers unless the author can justify them: the PR keeps a lot of incidental complexity when a code-judo move would delete it. Pushes a file from below 1000 lines to above 1000 lines. Adds ad-hoc branching that tangles an existing flow. Scatters feature checks across shared code. Adds an unnecessary abstraction, wrapper, or cast-heavy contract, or duplicates an existing helper or puts logic in the wrong layer when there is a clear canonical home. If those conditions are not met, leave explicit, actionable feedback and push for a cleaner decomposition.\n\n## Review Tone\n\nBe direct, serious, and demanding about quality. Do not be rude, but do not soften major maintainability issues into mild suggestions. If the code is making the codebase messier, say so. If the implementation missed an obvious dramatic simplification, say that too. Do not be satisfied with \"maybe rename this\" when the real issue is structural.\n\n\n## Instructions\n\nReview the code through every lens in the rubric and the code-quality lens above that you find relevant. Do not force lenses that don't apply. A simple bug fix does not need paragraphs about architectural integrity.\n\nFor each finding, provide:\n\n1. **Severity**: `critical` | `warning` | `nit`\n   - `critical`: Would cause bugs, data loss, security issues, or fundamentally broken behavior\n   - `warning`: Design concern, maintainability risk, or correctness issue that isn't immediately broken but will cause pain\n   - `nit`: Style, naming, minor improvement.\n2. **Finding**: What the problem is, in concrete terms. Reference specific lines/functions.\n3. **Evidence**: Why you believe this is a problem. Show your reasoning. Don't just assert.\n4. **Suggestion** (optional): What you'd do instead, if you have a concrete alternative. Skip this if you don't have a clear fix.\n\n## What Makes a Good Finding\n\n- It references specific code, not vague concerns (\"this could be better\")\n- It explains WHY something is a problem, not just THAT it is\n- It distinguishes between \"this is broken\" and \"I would have done this differently\"\n- It considers the stated intent. A finding that ignores the context of what's being built is a bad finding\n\n## What to Avoid\n\n- Restating what the code does without identifying a problem\n- Praising the code. You're an adversary, not a cheerleader. If you find nothing wrong, say \"no findings\" and stop.\n\n## Output\n\nReturn your findings as a structured list. If you have zero findings, say so. An empty review is a valid outcome.\n\n```\n## Findings\n\n### 1. [Severity] Short title\n**Location**: file:line or function name\n**Finding**: What's wrong\n**Evidence**: Why this matters\n**Suggestion**: (optional) What to do instead\n\n### 2. [Severity] Short title\n...\n```\n"

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "## Why\n\nCommas, quotation marks and line breaks in field values can shift CSV columns and records. Quote those values at the export boundary.\n\n## What changed\n\n- Quote fields containing commas, quotes, CR or LF, and double embedded quotes.\n- Preserve String conversion, row order, plain values and CRLF row separators.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Covers CSV string export only.\n- Leaves consumers, streaming and spreadsheet interpretation unchanged.\n\n## Tradeoffs\n\nQuote only fields that need escaping so plain-value output retains its existing form.\n\n## Blast Radius\n\nAll csv(rows) consumers receive escaped values for these characters. Empty exports and ordinary values retain their behavior.\n\n## Verification\n\n- [Base reproduction](04-patch-and-base-red.raw.json) failed the literal quoting assertion at the supplied baseline.\n- [Head checks](03-local-tools-and-head-tests.raw.json) passed one Bun test and three assertions.\n- [Scoped reviews](review-summary.md) found no issues; the external deslop gate remains unresolved.\n"

      "text": "{\n  \"clock\": \"2026-10-16T19:28:45.959Z\",\n  \"purpose\": \"Read-only operation metadata discovery only; no connector called\",\n  \"builtin\": {\n    \"name\": \"mcp__codex_apps__github_create_pull_request\",\n    \"description\": \"Access repositories, issues, and pull requests. Required for some features such as Codex\\n\\nOpen a pull request in the repository. Returns the connector's normalized PR snapshot, not the full REST response payload. Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#create-a-pull-request. This tool is part of plugin `GitHub`.\\n\\nexec tool declaration:\\n```ts\\ndeclare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__github_create_pull_request(args: {\\n  // GitHub REST `base` branch that the pull request targets.\\n  base?: string | null;\\n  // Compatibility alias for `base`, the target branch for the pull request.\\n  base_branch?: string | null;\\n  // Pull request description or summary. GitHub allows omitting this field.\\n  body?: string | null;\\n  // Create the pull request as a draft.\\n  draft?: boolean;\\n  // GitHub REST `head` branch containing the proposed changes.\\n  head?: string | null;\\n  // Compatibility alias for `head`, the branch containing the proposed changes.\\n  head_branch?: string | null;\\n  // Repository where the head branch lives. Required by GitHub for some same-organization cross-repository pull requests.\\n  head_repo?: string | null;\\n  // Existing issue number to convert into a pull request.\\n  issue?: number | null;\\n  // Whether maintainers may modify the pull request branch.\\n  maintainer_can_modify?: boolean | null;\\n  // Repository in `owner/name` form, such as `openai/openai`. This maps to GitHub REST `owner` and `repo` path parameters: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository\\n  repository_full_name: string;\\n  // Title for the new pull request. Required unless `issue` is supplied.\\n  title?: string | null;\\n}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };\\n```\"\n  },\n  \"externalActionPolicy\": \"All real PR operations forbidden; no interface invoked or forge service contacted\",\n  \"limitation\": \"Earlier in-memory metadata filter overmatched unrelated tool descriptions; no unrelated connector/account data read and broad metadata not included in artifact\"\n}\n"

    {
      "path": "grades/web-repairs/projections/draft-only-authorized/checklist.md",
      "bytes": 9268,
      "sha256": "1b193d2777e579fbe30fd19f44d1c9c5cf3cd92d2ec60e83504636b97e6b76b4",
      "owner": "web-013-fresh-repair-draft-only-authorized",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "### Opening a PR\n\nInvoked at the end of every other playbook.\n\nUse [session capabilities](../../../references/host-capabilities.md), [workflow ownership](../../../references/workflow-ownership.md), [model roles](../../../references/model-roles.md), and the [assignment contract](../../../references/orchestration-contract.md). These documents live at the package root. Prepare a reviewable title, body, verification artifacts, and intended base before any external operation. Record explicit authorization, the repository, branch head, destination and action identity. Check the destination after an interrupted action before any replay. Missing access or permission leaves the external action blocked and the content available locally. Draft-only permission permits a draft, never readiness, push, merge or comments.\n\n**Worktree.** Work from a git worktree off main. Subagents inherit it. Multiple independent workers on the same branch each get their own isolated worktree. Preserve unrelated dirty work before creating an authorized fresh worktree. Report a snarled worktree instead of resetting or discarding unowned changes. Missing independent workers permits an authorized sequential reduction, never a claim of independent review.\n\n**Commits.** Commit liberally within the authorized local scope. Rebase into small, ordered commits before opening PRs. Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit. New commit when separable.\n\n**PRs.** Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit if that external skill is exposed and authorized. It is not bundled here. If absent, disclose the missing slop-strip and leave that gate open and block creation until the required review gate is satisfied; do not install it or treat prose cleanup as equivalent. Run `/no-comments` through [no-comments](../../no-comments/SKILL.md) before review. Write every PR title, PR description, and commit body with `/technical-writing` through [technical-writing](../../technical-writing/SKILL.md), then apply `/unslop` through [unslop](../../unslop/SKILL.md). Apply every technical-writing layer except Diátaxis. Use one word for each action, keep articles, and avoid `-ing` when a plain verb works.\n\n**Titles.** Use Conventional Commits in the form `type(scope): subject`. Use `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, or `perf` as the type. Use the changed area, such as `pstack` or `poteto-mode`, as the scope. Keep the subject short and imperative. Name a real symbol when one carries the change. For example, `fix(pstack): retarget opening-a-pr babysit trigger`. Do not add a trailing period.\n\n**Descriptions.** The PR body is a briefing, not the lab notebook. A reviewer who has the diff should learn why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, and how you proved it works, in under a minute. Write short, simple sentences with few identifiers. Do not write walls of text. The squash commit body is the PR body. If the body would make the squash commit longer than about 40 lines, cut the body.\n\nPut each section under a `##` heading, not a bold lead-in, so the sections stand apart. Use these sections in order. Drop a section when it has nothing to say.\n\n- `## Why` gives the problem and the approach in one to three short sentences. Do not list SHAs or rebase genealogy. Do not add a \"based on main\" preamble.\n- `## What changed` has one to three short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.\n- `## Scope` always names what the PR covers and what it deliberately leaves out, for example a related follow-up or a known gap. Use one to three short items. Do not list symbols or paths, and do not write a file-by-file essay.\n- `## Tradeoffs` names only rejected alternatives that a reviewer would otherwise ask about. Skip this section when there was no real choice.\n- `## Blast Radius` gives one or two sentences on who or what the change touches and why that is safe or risky. If main is red, state the cost of leaving it red.\n- `## Verification` has one to three bullets. Each bullet names a real run path and its outcome. For a performance change, report one primary number with its unit in `before → after` form. Link the arena or swarm directory for the remaining evidence. Do not include sample-size methodology, swarm recitals, or metric tables.\n\nAfter these sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Do not paste full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, or \"CLEAN\" verdicts. Put these details in a linked artifact. A commit body does not restate its subject.\n\n**Forge.** Resolve the forge before the first PR operation and keep that choice for create, edit, view, watch, and merge. GitHub CLI (`gh`) is the default. If `command -v origin` succeeds and Origin can resolve the repository, prefer `origin pr ...`. If Origin is absent or cannot resolve the repository, stay on `gh` and record the fallback. Do not require Graphite (`gt`).\n\n**Built-in PR tool.** When the run provides a built-in PR tool, create, edit, retarget, and mark ready through it, never through a forge CLI. Its exposed instructions define the actual interface. An unavailable, denied or failed tool is a stated blocker, not permission to bypass its tracking through a CLI. A PR made with the CLI misses what the tool tracks, such as a description later runs can edit. Use the resolved forge for everything the tool does not cover, and for every PR operation when the run has no such tool.\n\n**Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch. Without a built-in PR tool, create a child with `origin pr create --status open --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` according to the resolved forge, and retarget an existing child with `origin pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` or `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work.\n\n**Readiness.** The source workflow opens every PR ready, never as a draft, when readiness is explicitly authorized. If only draft creation is authorized, preserve that limit and create a draft through the exposed tool or `gh pr create --draft`. Verify the actual draft state and report the readiness gate open. Use Origin draft creation only when its current interface supports it. Otherwise report blocked. All readiness instructions below require readiness authorization. A built-in PR tool can default to draft, so use its observed ready-creation interface, such as `draft: false` only when that field is actually supported. With Origin, pass `--status open`. With `gh`, omit `--draft`. If a PR still opens as a draft, mark it ready through the PR tool, or run `origin pr ready <number>` or `gh pr ready <number>` according to the resolved forge. Run `origin pr view <number>` or `gh pr view <number>` before you refer to PR status.\n\n**Babysit.** Opening a PR does not start a babysit. Post the URL and keep building. Finish the phase or stack first. Run a separate babysit pass only when the user asks for one after the whole stack exists. A babysit for each new PR stalls the build and spends checks on commits that later waves restart. Push back when feedback drifts from intent.\n\nA subagent that opens a PR runs `interrogate` through [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md), `/deslop`, and `/no-comments`, and posts the URL. Then it returns to the parent without babysitting, unless it is an Autopilot-full or Autopilot-stack owner. That owner's brief assigns the babysit loop and is the ask [babysit](babysit.md) waits for. The owner starts the loop after its code-ready report and reports merge-ready or STACK-READY as its playbook says. The rules here and in [babysit](babysit.md) that hold babysitting until a whole stack is built do not apply to that owner.\n\nFor the owner exception, read [Autopilot-full](autopilot-full.md) or [Autopilot-stack](autopilot-stack.md) and the [Bugbot triage rubric](../references/bugbot-triage.md). These briefs assign babysitting only within explicit user authorization and observed capabilities. Opening a PR alone never supplies that authorization. No watcher, bootstrap or orchestration helper runs in this opening step. Babysit owns the actual watcher binding.\n\n\nTask-specific authorization and checkpoint before work:\n- Only local draft and review preparation. No real PR or other external action.\n- Existing supplied base/head history and actual source.patch define scope. No native commits, worktree history mutation or push.\n- Full Comment Sicko first-response gate before its reads/tools, then independent adversarial pair after comment review.\n- Blocking first steps. Verify actual input HEAD/base/patch bytes and real Bun gates.\n- Independent workstreams. Reviewers use disjoint outputs; root alone owns draft.\n- Shared mutable state. Source remains unchanged; only admin reports/draft owned writes.\n- Smallest safe decomposition. One draft coordinator, one Comment Sicko, then one required reviewer pair.\n"
    },

      "sha256": "2daf05ff6b2b313a165101457469c9b84b4abe9b90221107f559403e27831456",
